title: Clicks, comments, consequences: Are content creators’ socio-structural and platform characteristics shaping the exposure to negative sentiment, offensive language, and hate speech on YouTube?
reasoning: The paper includes religious affiliation as a primary socio-structural variable in its research framework. It specifically investigates whether a content creator's religion (or lack of identifiable affiliation) correlates with their exposure to negative sentiment and hate speech, formalizing this in hypothesis H4 and testing it through multiple OLS regression models.
